claims.text: The initial alloy is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperature.
High-temperature oxidation of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr causes embrittlement and degradation of mechanical performance.
The proposed intervention is an approximately 50 nm Al2O3 coating deposited by atomic layer deposition.
The proposed coating includes an adhesion-promoting interlayer, such as a gradient TiO2 layer.
The adhesion-promoting interlayer will mitigate thermal-expansion mismatch between the coating and alloy.
The coating system will form a continuous, dense, and adherent Al2O3 barrier.
The adhesion-promoting interlayer will maintain coating integrity and resist spallation during thermal cycling.
The Al2O3 coating will retard oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature exposure.
Retarding oxygen ingress will prevent deleterious oxide-phase formation in the alloy.
Preventing deleterious oxide formation will preserve the alloy's tensile ductility and yield strength.
After 100 hours at 1000 °C in air or an oxygen-rich atmosphere, the coated alloy will have less oxygen ingress and thinner oxide layers than an untreated control.
After the specified exposure, the coated alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility within the original 8–16% range.
After the specified exposure, the coated alloy will retain a 1000 °C yield strength within 163–530 MPa when tested at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed exposure condition is 1000 °C in air or an oxygen-rich atmosphere for 100 hours.
Mechanical testing will be performed at room temperature and 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
